To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MTD of a gemcitabine-based chemotherapy in combination with the mTOR inhibitor everolimus is 400 mg/week gemcitibine plus 5 mg/day everolimus and that this combination is well tolerated.
the combination of low-dose gemcicabine and everolimus is safe and effective for the treatment of advanced pancreatic cancer.

we determined the maximum tolerated dose and dose-limiting toxicities of a combination of the mTOR-inhibition with everolimus and a low-dose chemotherapy in patients with advanced and/or metastasized pancreatic carcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the treatment of advanced pancreatic cancer.
the treatment of pancreatic cancer with a combination of everolimus and gemcitabines.
the combination of everolimus and gemcitabines in pancreatic cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of gemcitabine 400 mg/week and everolimus 5 mg/d was well tolerated and the recommended phase II dose for future clinical trials in pancreatic cancer patients.
the combination of everolimus and gemcitabines was well tolerated and that the MTD for this combination was 5 mg/m2 gemcitabine and 10 mg everolimis.
the combination of everolimus and gemcitabene is a promising approach for the treatment of patients with advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of everolimus with a low-dose of gemcitabine was well tolerated and showed a promising antitumour activity in patients with advanced and/or metastasized pancreatic cancer.
the combination of gemcitabine and everolimus is feasible in advanced pancreatic cancer patients.
the combination of everolimus and gemcitabines is safe and tolerable in patients with advanced or metastatic pancreatic cancer.

everolimus and gemcitabines combination therapy is safe and tolerable.
the combination of low-dose gemcita­bine with everolimus is safe and well tolerated in advanced pancreatic cancer patients.
